Starting to learn anatomy can be overwhelming, but it shouldn't be. Daily Anatomy can be used without any prior knowledge. It starts with the basics, and challenges your brain more and more over time. Learning with  Daily Anatomy is not only about repetition. It introduces information in varying forms. With Daily Anatomy you learn all the important structures of human anatomy. This includes bones, muscles, nerves, vessels and specific points on the bones.

Instead of many thin arrows pointing at various structures, each structure is clearly highlighted in green in its entirety. This way you can easily identify and memorize both shape and location.

*How to stay motivated and not forget*

Whether you need to learn lists of information, or for instance, every muscle and bone in the human body including how they function together, there is a method really works to help you out. The bonus is that this method doesn't stress you out either because you get to take lots of breaks.

It's called spaced repetition, and it's the way to go for knowledge that sticks in your cranium.

By using spaced repetition, you work through a series of increasing intervals of time between studying what you've previously learned. This method utilizes the psychological spacing effect, which occurs when you are going back over information that you have already learned in order to remember it better. Spaced repetition works well for lists of items or new vocabularies such as medical terminology.

Major depressive disorder, or depression, is a mood disorder characterized by a significant drop in mood, as well as other symptoms, including feelings of hopelessness, guilt, fatigue, irregular eating habits, rumination, and/or suicidal thoughts. The disorder causes a significant impairment in the daily life of those whom it effects. However, it is treatable with medication and/or psychotherapy.

Symptoms of depression
The symptoms of depression can vary from person to person. Some common symptoms include:
● feeling down, guilty, or hopeless 
● unhealthy appetite 
● poor sleep 
● trouble focusing 

What Can This App Do For Me? 
The Depression Screening Test app is specifically developed to give you a general sense of if your symptoms align with the symptoms of major depressive disorder. It is not a diagnostic test, and you should always consult with your doctor before making any decisions based on information given in this app. The Depression Screening Test utilizes the widely recognized PHQ-9 test to gauge your symptoms and determine if they align with those of major depressive disorder. The Test also allows you to save your results via a graph and chart that can show trends in your results over time. 

FAQ About Depression - 

How Is Depression Different From Feeling Down?
Depression is different from feeling down in that it is a mental health condition that causes significant distress and often interferes with a person’s ability to function in daily life. People with major depressive disorder often have systemwide symptoms, including concentration issues, suicidal thoughts, lack of interest in daily activities, etc., and this can last for months to years. 

While everyone has bad days where they may feel emotionally down or depressed, they do not feel the same level of distress or interference with daily life that people with major depressive disorder experience. 
 
How Is Depression Treated?
Depression can be treated with the help of therapy, whereas some other treatments are also effective in this regard. All these remedies are given below:
 
1. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) 
One type of therapy that is particularly effective for treating depression is CBT. CBT is a form of psychotherapy which helps one to break negative thought patterns and set goals for their recovery. 
2. Medications
In some cases, medications may also be prescribed to help treat major depressive disorder. Commonly prescribed medications include SSRIs and SNRIs. Examples of these medications include Sertraline, Fluoxetine, Paroxetine, and Bupropion. Medications can be an effective treatment for depression when combined with therapy. People with major depressive disorder should always consult a mental health professional to determine if medication is right for them.
3. Therapist Consultation
If you are experiencing symptoms of depression, it is important to consult with a mental health professional to discuss your treatment options. A therapist can help work with you to develop a customized treatment plan that meets your needs.
4. Self-Care
There are also several things that you can do on your own to help manage your depression symptoms. These self-care strategies include :
• Identifying and challenging your negative thoughts
• Practicing relaxation techniques
• Avoiding triggers that exacerbate your symptoms
• Exercising regularly
• Getting enough sleep
 
Major depressive disorder is a treatable condition, but it often requires a combination of therapy and medication to be effectively managed. Living with depression can be difficult, but there are treatments available that can help you manage your symptoms and improve your quality of life. If you are struggling with depression, contact a mental health professional for help. Always consult a doctor or mental health professional in case of severe symptoms first.

Los antimicrobianos son un grupo muy amplio de fármacos extraordinariamente eficaces y complejos. Desde su descubrimiento hace 70 años, han salvado millones de vidas y permitido avances médicos, convirtiéndose en medicamentos indispensables para el tratamiento de la mayoría de los procesos infecciosos bacterianos.

El desarrollo de resistencias a los antimicrobianos, la aparición y diseminación de bacterias multirresistentes y la escasez de tratamientos alternativos, son uno de los mayores problemas de salud pública en la actualidad. Aunque son muchos los factores que favorecen la selección y diseminación de la resistencia a los antibióticos, el uso inapropiado e indiscriminado de los mismos es uno de los factores principales que contribuyen a este fenómeno.

La utilización de antimicrobianos en el medio hospitalario es mejorable en el 30-50% de los casos. La existencia de microorganismos resistentes y su variabilidad entre hospitales e incluso dentro de las diferentes áreas de un mismo hospital hace necesario un buen conocimiento de la epidemiología microbiológica local. La selección óptima del antimicrobiano y su posología en los diferentes síndromes infecciosos requieren también una formación específica y actualizada.

Con el ánimo de promover una utilización más adecuada de los antimicrobianos la Comisión de Infección Hospitalaria del Hospital Son Espases (Palma de Mallorca, España) ha actualizado con esta tercera edición los protocolos de actuación en enfermedades infecciosas.

Con el formato app del manual de protocolos queremos facilitar la difusión y utilización de estos protocolos, y hacerlos accesibles y de fácil lectura para que resulten de utilidad en la práctica clínica diaria. También se puede acceder a los protocolos completos con su bibliografía desde la página de inicio para un estudio más detenido.

La aplicación va destinada a los médicos y farmacéuticos en general, y comprende tanto aspectos generales del uso de antimicrobianos (prevención de la aparición de resistencias, dosificación en insuficiencia renal y hepática, dosificación en pacientes obesos, farmacocinética y farmacodinámica, etc), como guías concretas de tratamiento por aparatos (respiratorio, digestivo, urinario, etc). Hay que tener en cuenta que se trata de recomendaciones locales basadas en las situaciones específicas de nuestro centro y en la información de sensibilidad antibiótica aportada por el Servicio de Microbiología del Hospital Son Espases, por lo que algunas de las recomendaciones deben ser interpretadas y adaptadas a la ubicación del lector.

También hemos querido facilitar el acceso a otros recursos como calculadoras clínicas, cursos y casos clínicos. Esta es la descripción de todas las funcionalidades de la aplicación:

- Lectura off-line de los aspectos generales del uso de antimicrobianos, de los protocolos de tratamiento, y de los protocolos de profilaxis.
